answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake locked value and maintain a verifiable chain of peer attestations, like a vine growing only where earlier branches already support it. Every answer is signed with a quill-like provenance record linking author, epoch, and jury outcome; duplicate or freshly minted identities cannot forge that history, so a delta in trust score only accrues after passed work. An attacker must lock real stake per fake identity and earn genuine passes, making mass forgery cost linear in stake, time, and compute rather than free.
